GIF: Graphics Interchange Format, an image format

GPS: Global Positioning System, the satellite system phones use to know where they are

HSTS: HTTP strict transport security, a header requiring HTTPS

IDOR: insecure direct object reference, reading someone else's record by changing an ID

IEEE: Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers, the body behind standards such as IEEE 754 floating point

IP: internet protocol; also intellectual property: legal ownership of inventions, designs, brands and creative work

ISR: incremental static regeneration, rebuilding static pages after deploy

JPEG: Joint Photographic Experts Group, the common photo format

KCL: Kirchhoff’s current law: the currents into a node sum to zero

KUKA: a German maker of industrial robot arms
KVL: Kirchhoff’s voltage law: the voltages around a loop sum to zero

LSP: Liskov substitution principle, the L in SOLID

LVDT: linear variable differential transformer, a sensor for measuring linear position

MDC: mapped diagnostic context, per-thread values added to every Java log line

MRR: mean reciprocal rank: 1 for a right result ranked first, 1/2 for second, and so on, averaged

NDC: normalised device coordinates, the [-1, 1] cube after the perspective divide

NR: Newton–Raphson, the inverse-kinematics method Δθ = J⁻¹Δx (fast but fragile near singularities)

OCR: optical character recognition, reading text from an image

PHP: PHP: Hypertext Preprocessor, a server-side scripting language
PII: personally identifiable information, data that identifies a person directly or in combination
PKCE: proof key for code exchange, protecting OAuth logins in apps that can't keep a secret
PKCS: Public-Key Cryptography Standards, a family of formats such as PKCS#12
PKI: public key infrastructure, the system of certificates and authorities
PLC: programmable logic controller, a rugged industrial computer for controlling machinery
PNG: Portable Network Graphics, a lossless image format
POODLE: Padding Oracle On Downgraded Legacy Encryption (an attack)
POSIX: Portable Operating System Interface, the standard Unix programming interface
PPM: portable pixmap, a plain-text image format
PR: pull request; also service by priority (a queue discipline that serves the most important customer first)

RAND: the RAND Corporation, a US research institute (from 'research and development')

RED: rate, errors, duration, the request-centric monitoring signals

SLA: service level agreement, a contractual reliability promise

SMS: short message service, a text message

SPF: Sender Policy Framework, a DNS record listing who may send a domain's email

SRP: single responsibility principle, the S in SOLID
SSE: server-sent events, a way for a server to stream messages to a client over one HTTP response

SYN: synchronise, the TCP flag that opens a connection

TBRL: top, bottom, right, left: the bit order of a Cohen-Sutherland region code

PVC: polyvinyl chloride, a thermoplastic used for pipes
QFD: quality function deployment, turning customer needs into specific design requirements

CF: cash flow, money coming in or going out in a period
CM: contribution margin, selling price minus variable cost
CPI: consumer price index, a measure of the prices households pay; also cost performance index (earned value analysis): earned value divided by actual cost; below 1 means over budget

ECO: course-code prefix for economics, as printed on the 2025/2026 GEG 501 paper

FV: future value, what a present sum grows to when invested
FW: future worth, a project's cash flows moved to the end of its life
GDP: gross domestic product, the total value of goods and services an economy produces

MOS: margin of safety, how far sales can fall before a loss

MU: marginal utility, the extra satisfaction from one more unit

NPW: net present worth, another name for net present value

PPI: producer price index, a measure of the prices producers receive

XYZ: a placeholder name, as in a made-up firm called XYZ in an example question

TNOW: the clock time of the current step, a column in a Brooks' algorithm table
TSCHED: the time an activity is actually scheduled to start, a column in a Brooks' algorithm table
CFAA: Computer Fraud and Abuse Act, the primary US federal law against unauthorised computer access
CMA: Computer Misuse Act, the UK law against unauthorised computer access
RoE: rules of engagement, the signed document that defines what a pentest may and may not touch
CVSS: Common Vulnerability Scoring System, a 0–10 score for how severe a vulnerability is
SIEM: security information and event management, a system that collects logs and alerts on attacks
OSINT: open-source intelligence, information gathered from public sources
CTF: capture the flag, a legal hacking competition or practice platform
CVE: Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures, a public catalogue of known vulnerabilities with an id each
BOLA: broken object level authorization, letting a user reach another user's data by changing an id
BFLA: broken function level authorization, letting a user call a function (such as an admin route) they shouldn't
PoC: proof of concept, the smallest demonstration that a vulnerability really works
MSA: master service agreement, the overall contract a pentest's scope hangs off
SOW: statement of work, the document that defines a specific engagement's scope and deliverables
VDP: vulnerability disclosure programme, a published way to report security bugs to an organisation
CIDR: classless inter-domain routing, the a.b.c.d/n way of writing a range of IP addresses
WPA2: Wi-Fi Protected Access 2, a Wi-Fi encryption standard
WPA3: Wi-Fi Protected Access 3, the newer Wi-Fi encryption standard
PTES: Penetration Testing Execution Standard, a common pentest methodology
OSSTMM: Open Source Security Testing Methodology Manual
SP: Special Publication, the NIST document series (e.g. SP 800-115)
DVWA: Damn Vulnerable Web Application, a deliberately-insecure app for practice
WHOIS: a public record of who registered a domain, when, and through which company
LDAP: Lightweight Directory Access Protocol, used for directory services and logins
WAF: web application firewall, a filter in front of a web app that blocks malicious-looking requests
CEH: Certified Ethical Hacker, a broad, conceptual pentest certification
CIA: confidentiality, integrity, availability — the three things security protects
OSCP: Offensive Security Certified Professional, a hands-on pentest certification with a practical exam
ZAP: Zed Attack Proxy, OWASP’s free intercepting-proxy web-testing tool
BSSID: basic service set identifier, a Wi-Fi access point’s unique hardware address
EDR: endpoint detection and response, security software that watches devices for attacks
PSK: pre-shared key, the Wi-Fi passphrase shared by everyone on the network
SAE: Simultaneous Authentication of Equals, WPA3’s handshake that resists offline cracking
SSID: service set identifier, a Wi-Fi network’s name
HTB: Hack The Box, a platform of legal, intentionally-vulnerable practice machines
THM: TryHackMe, a guided platform of legal practice machines
WPS: Wi-Fi Protected Setup, an 8-digit-PIN shortcut for joining a network, with a known design flaw
FTP: File Transfer Protocol, an old protocol for transferring files
PI: proportional-integral, a controller type that acts on the error now and on its running total
PD: proportional-derivative, a controller type that acts on the error and its rate of change; also powered device (Power over Ethernet)
RLC: resistor-inductor-capacitor, as in an RLC circuit
RL: reinforcement learning; also resistor-inductor, as in an RL circuit
LC: inductor-capacitor, as in an LC circuit
PM: phase margin (control): how much extra phase lag a loop can take before it goes unstable; also post meridiem (afternoon)
GM: gain margin (control): how many times the loop gain can grow before the loop goes unstable; also geometric mean, as in the AM–GM inequality
MIT: Massachusetts Institute of Technology; also the MIT licence, a permissive open-source licence
LQ: linear quadratic: a linear plant with a quadratic cost, as in LQ optimal control
LQG: linear quadratic Gaussian: an LQR controller combined with a Kalman filter
MIMO: multiple input, multiple output: a system (or radio link) with several inputs and several outputs
SISO: single input, single output: a system with one input and one output
DAC: digital-to-analogue converter; also discretionary access control (security)
BIBO: bounded input, bounded output: a system is BIBO stable if no bounded input can make its output grow without limit
EKF: extended Kalman filter: a Kalman filter that linearises a nonlinear model at every step
UKF: unscented Kalman filter: a Kalman filter that pushes sigma points through a nonlinear model instead of linearising it
PBH: Popov–Belevitch–Hautus, a rank test for controllability and observability
MRAC: model reference adaptive control: adjusting a controller online so the plant behaves like a chosen reference model
LTR: loop transfer recovery: detuning a Kalman filter so an LQG loop regains the margins of LQR
ITAE: integral of time-weighted absolute error, a performance index used to choose pole locations
DT: discrete time (control and signals); also data type
CBF: control barrier function: a function that gives a provable condition keeping a system inside a safe set
VPN: virtual private network, an encrypted tunnel between two points over an untrusted network
IPS: intrusion prevention system, a tool in the traffic path that blocks traffic matching attack rules
NIDS: network-based intrusion detection system, an IDS that watches traffic on a network segment
HIDS: host-based intrusion detection system, an IDS that runs on one machine and watches its files, logs and processes
IPsec: Internet Protocol Security, a set of protocols that encrypts traffic at the IP layer, common for site-to-site VPNs
VLAN: virtual local area network, a way to split one physical network into separate logical networks
DMZ: demilitarized zone, a network segment for internet-facing servers, kept apart from the internal network
NGFW: next-generation firewall, a firewall that also understands applications and often includes intrusion prevention
UFW: Uncomplicated Firewall, a simple front end for the Linux firewall on Ubuntu and Debian
IoT: Internet of Things, everyday devices on a network, like smart bulbs and cameras
SOC: security operations centre, the team that watches alerts and responds to attacks
RDP: Remote Desktop Protocol, Microsoft's protocol for controlling a Windows machine over the network
NAS: network-attached storage, a file server on your network
PC: personal computer, a desktop or laptop
QR: quick response, as in QR code: a square barcode a phone camera can read
SIM: subscriber identity module, the card (or eSIM) that ties a phone number to a phone
TOTP: time-based one-time password, the 6-digit code an authenticator app shows, changing every 30 seconds
SSL: Secure Sockets Layer, the old, broken predecessor of TLS; people still say "SSL certificate"
ACME: Automatic Certificate Management Environment, the protocol Let's Encrypt uses to issue certificates automatically
APT: advanced persistent threat, a well-funded, often government-backed group that attacks patiently and stays hidden
BLAKE2: a fast, secure cryptographic hash function, an alternative to SHA-256
BLAKE3: a newer, very fast cryptographic hash function from the BLAKE family
CRL: certificate revocation list, a CA's published list of certificates it has cancelled
CSPRNG: cryptographically secure pseudo-random number generator, a random generator safe for keys and tokens
CSR: certificate signing request, a public key and name sent to a CA, signed to prove you hold the private key
DH: Diffie–Hellman, a way for two parties to agree a shared secret over a public channel
ECB: Electronic Codebook, a block-cipher mode that encrypts each block alone and leaks patterns; never use it
ECC: elliptic-curve cryptography, public-key cryptography with much smaller keys than RSA for the same strength
KDF: key derivation function, a function that turns a password or shared secret into a proper key
OAEP: Optimal Asymmetric Encryption Padding, the random padding RSA encryption must use
PBKDF2: Password-Based Key Derivation Function 2, a slow, salted way to turn a password into a key
STRIDE: spoofing, tampering, repudiation, information disclosure, denial of service, elevation of privilege: a threat-modelling checklist
BEC: business email compromise, a scam email impersonating a boss or supplier to get a payment made or bank details changed
BVN: bank verification number, the identity number tied to a Nigerian bank customer
DAI: dynamic ARP inspection, a managed-switch feature that drops forged ARP replies
MITM: man in the middle, an attacker secretly placed between two parties, reading or changing their traffic
WEP: Wired Equivalent Privacy, the original, now broken, Wi-Fi encryption; replaced by WPA2 and WPA3
ASLR: address space layout randomization, a defence that randomizes memory locations to make overflow exploits harder
RAT: remote access trojan, malware that gives the attacker full remote control of a machine
ATT: part of MITRE ATT&CK, a public knowledge base of real-world attacker tactics and techniques
CK: part of MITRE ATT&CK, a public knowledge base of real-world attacker tactics and techniques
MITRE: the non-profit that maintains the ATT&CK knowledge base of attacker tactics and techniques
IOC: indicator of compromise, an artefact of an attack such as a malicious IP, domain or file hash
SOAR: security orchestration, automation and response, tooling that automates repetitive incident-response steps
XDR: extended detection and response, EDR broadened across endpoint, network and cloud
SANS: a security training and certification institute; here, its incident-response process
RHEL: Red Hat Enterprise Linux, a Linux distribution
CIS: Center for Internet Security, which publishes system-hardening benchmarks
IR: incident response, the planned process for handling a security incident
DFIR: digital forensics and incident response, the combined investigative discipline
EICAR: a harmless standard antivirus test file that every scanner detects by agreement
SPL: Search Processing Language, the query language used by Splunk
PICERL: preparation, identification, containment, eradication, recovery, lessons learned — the incident-response phases
MISP: an open-source threat-intelligence platform for sharing indicators of compromise
PE32: the 32-bit Portable Executable format, the structure of a Windows .exe file
B2B: business to business, companies selling to other companies rather than to consumers
CSF: Cybersecurity Framework (NIST), organised around Identify, Protect, Detect, Respond and Recover
DSS: Data Security Standard; in PCI-DSS, the standard for handling payment-card data
PCI: Payment Card Industry; in PCI-DSS, the security standard for handling payment-card data
GRC: governance, risk and compliance, the management side of security
HIPAA: Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act, the US law protecting healthcare data
IEC: International Electrotechnical Commission, co-publisher of standards such as ISO/IEC 27001
ISMS: information security management system, the documented policies and processes ISO 27001 certifies
CISA: Certified Information Systems Auditor, an audit-focused security certification; also the US Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency
CISM: Certified Information Security Manager, a management-focused security certification
CISO: chief information security officer, the senior-most security role, owning the security program
CISSP: Certified Information Systems Security Professional, the flagship senior security certification
GCFA: GIAC Certified Forensic Analyst, a digital-forensics certification
GCIH: GIAC Certified Incident Handler, an incident-response certification
GPEN: GIAC Penetration Tester, a pentesting certification
GWAPT: GIAC Web Application Penetration Tester, a web-application pentest certification
PNPT: Practical Network Penetration Tester, a hands-on pentest certification
HVAC: heating, ventilation and air conditioning; here, the contractor whose access led to Target's 2013 breach
SBOM: software bill of materials, a complete inventory of every component in a piece of software
SCA: software composition analysis, scanning software dependencies for known vulnerabilities
SLSA: Supply-chain Levels for Software Artifacts, a framework for build provenance and integrity
ARN: Amazon Resource Name, the unique identifier of an AWS resource such as a bucket or role
CIEM: cloud infrastructure entitlement management, tooling that continuously analyses who can do what and flags over-permissioning
CNAPP: cloud-native application protection platform, consolidating posture, entitlement, workload and runtime security
CRM: customer relationship management, software for tracking customers and sales
CSPM: cloud security posture management, tooling that continuously checks a running cloud for misconfigurations
GCS: Google Cloud Storage, Google's object-storage service
OPA: Open Policy Agent, a policy-as-code engine used to enforce security guardrails
AFL: American Fuzzy Lop, a fuzzer that feeds a program millions of mutated inputs to find crashes
AMD: Advanced Micro Devices, a maker of processors (CPUs)
APP: authorised push payment; APP fraud is a scam where you are tricked into transferring money yourself
ASU: Arizona State University, which runs the free pwn.college course
CET: Control-flow Enforcement Technology, a processor feature that keeps a protected shadow copy of return addresses to block ROP
CFI: control-flow integrity, a defence that checks every jump and call goes somewhere the program legitimately could
DEP: Data Execution Prevention, Windows' name for marking data memory (stack, heap) as not runnable; the same idea as NX
GEF: GDB Enhanced Features, a plugin that makes the GDB debugger friendlier for exploit work
GOT: Global Offset Table, a table of addresses a program uses to find library functions like printf at run time
IC3: the FBI's Internet Crime Complaint Center, where US internet fraud is reported
IDA: Interactive Disassembler, a commercial tool for reading compiled programs
JOP: jump-oriented programming, like ROP but chaining code snippets that end in jumps instead of returns
NCMEC: the US National Center for Missing & Exploited Children, which runs the Take It Down service for minors
NX: no-execute, a defence that marks memory as either writable or runnable, never both, so injected code can't run
PLT: Procedure Linkage Table, small stubs a program calls that jump through the GOT to reach library functions
RAX: a 64-bit x86 register that holds a function's return value (and the system-call number)
RBP: the 64-bit x86 base pointer register, which marks the base of the current stack frame
RDI: a 64-bit x86 register that carries the first argument to a function
RDX: a 64-bit x86 register that carries the third argument to a function
RELRO: relocation read-only, a defence that makes the GOT read-only so attackers can't overwrite it
RIP: the 64-bit x86 instruction pointer, the register holding the address of the next instruction to run
ROP: return-oriented programming, chaining small pieces of a program's existing code (gadgets) through return addresses
RSI: a 64-bit x86 register that carries the second argument to a function
RSP: the 64-bit x86 stack pointer, the register holding the address of the top of the stack
UAF: use-after-free, a bug where a program keeps using memory after giving it back
ACL: access control list, the list of who holds which rights over an object (in AD, dangerous rights like WriteDACL or GenericAll are escalation paths)
ADCS: Active Directory Certificate Services, Microsoft's PKI; misconfigured certificate templates (the ESC family) let a low-privilege user get a certificate that authenticates as an admin
AS: Authentication Service, the part of the Kerberos KDC that issues your first ticket (the TGT) — the AS-REQ/AS-REP exchange
REQ: request, the client's half of a Kerberos message pair, as in AS-REQ and TGS-REQ
REP: reply, the KDC's half of a Kerberos message pair, as in AS-REP and TGS-REP
TGS: Ticket-Granting Service, the Kerberos exchange that issues a service ticket; also the service ticket itself
TGT: Ticket-Granting Ticket, your proof-of-login Kerberos ticket, encrypted with the KRBTGT account's hash
KDC: Key Distribution Center, the Kerberos service (running on the Domain Controller) that issues tickets
KRBTGT: the special Active Directory account whose password hash encrypts every TGT; knowing it lets an attacker forge tickets forever, so it is the domain's master key
SPN: Service Principal Name, a label like MSSQLSvc/db.corp.local that links a running service to the account behind it; you request a Kerberos ticket for a service by its SPN
NTLM: NT LAN Manager, an older Windows authentication scheme that proves knowledge of the password hash directly — which is why a stolen hash can be used as-is (pass-the-hash)
DA: Domain Admin, shorthand for a member of the group that controls the whole domain
OU: Organizational Unit, a folder inside an AD domain for grouping objects so policy can be applied to them together
GPO: Group Policy Object, a bundle of settings and scripts AD pushes to machines; controlling one runs code on every machine it applies to
GPP: Group Policy Preferences, an older Group Policy feature whose cpassword bug stored an encrypted password with a publicly known key
IIS: Internet Information Services, Microsoft's web server; often run under a service account
SMB: Server Message Block, the Windows file-sharing and remote-admin protocol (also used by PsExec and NTLM relay)
WMI: Windows Management Instrumentation, a Windows remote-management interface often used for quiet lateral movement
DCOM: Distributed Component Object Model, a Windows remote-execution mechanism used as an alternative lateral-movement path
LSASS: Local Security Authority Subsystem Service, the Windows process that holds logged-in users' credentials in memory; dumping it is how mimikatz harvests credentials
SAM: Security Account Manager, the local database of account password hashes on a Windows machine
SYSTEM: the built-in Windows account with full local privileges (NT AUTHORITY\SYSTEM)
DPAPI: Data Protection API, the Windows system for encrypting saved secrets (browser passwords, Wi-Fi keys, RDP credentials) that an attacker with access can decrypt
LLMNR: Link-Local Multicast Name Resolution, a legacy Windows name-lookup protocol; poisoning it (with Responder) captures NTLM hashes off the wire
NBT: NetBIOS over TCP/IP (NBT-NS, the NetBIOS Name Service), another legacy name-lookup protocol abused like LLMNR to capture hashes
RSAT: Remote Server Administration Tools, the Windows feature that provides the Active Directory PowerShell module and management consoles
RBCD: Resource-Based Constrained Delegation, a modern escalation: abuse GenericWrite over a computer object to configure delegation to it and impersonate any user to its services
PRT: Primary Refresh Token, the Entra ID (Azure AD) credential that, if stolen, lets an attacker act as the user in the cloud
LAPS: Local Administrator Password Solution, a Microsoft tool that gives each machine a unique random local-admin password, so one stolen hash owns one box, not the fleet
ESC1: the first in the ESC1–ESC16 family of Active Directory Certificate Services (ADCS) template misconfigurations that allow privilege escalation
ESC16: the sixteenth in the ESC1–ESC16 family of Active Directory Certificate Services (ADCS) template misconfigurations
SAN: Subject Alternative Name, a certificate field; in ADCS abuse, controlling it lets a requested certificate authenticate as another user
GOAD: Game of Active Directory, a free, deliberately vulnerable AD lab you run yourself to practise the attacks
RE: reverse engineering, working backward from a compiled program to understand what it does
PE: Portable Executable, the Windows executable format (.exe/.dll) where most malware lives; its import table is a strong behavioural tell
PEB: Process Environment Block, a Windows in-memory structure a program can read — including a flag malware checks to detect a debugger
OEP: original entry point, the moment a packer finishes unpacking and the real code begins — the point to dump memory at
DLL: Dynamic Link Library, a Windows shared-code file (.dll); also the target of DLL injection and DLL hijacking
COM: Component Object Model, a Windows system for software components; COM hijacking is a persistence technique
CLR: Common Language Runtime, the .NET virtual machine; .NET binaries decompile almost back to source (e.g. with dnSpy)
DEX: Dalvik Executable, the Android bytecode format; jadx turns it into readable Java
DGA: Domain Generation Algorithm, malware that generates many pseudo-random C2 domains daily so defenders can't just block one address
AV: antivirus, software that detects and blocks malware (historically by signature)
NOP: no-operation, a CPU instruction that does nothing; patching a check to NOPs is a way to disable it
UPX: Ultimate Packer for eXecutables, a common, legitimate packer that is trivial to reverse (`upx -d`)
YARA: the standard language and tool for writing pattern-matching rules that identify malware families
NSA: the United States National Security Agency, which built and released the free Ghidra reverse-engineering tool
GDB: the GNU Debugger, the standard debugger on Linux (often extended with pwndbg or GEF)
CAPE: Config And Payload Extraction, an open-source automated malware sandbox (a fork of Cuckoo)
CFF: CFF Explorer, a Windows tool for inspecting and editing PE headers, imports and resources
FLARE: the reverse-engineering team at Mandiant, whose FLARE VM bundles Windows malware-analysis tools
DMCA: the US Digital Millennium Copyright Act, whose §1201 restricts bypassing copy protection (with narrow research exemptions)
DRM: Digital Rights Management, copy-protection technology; it uses the same hard obfuscation as serious malware
NG: next generation, as in FakeNet-NG, the tool that simulates the internet for a malware lab
API1: OWASP API Security Top 10 risk #1 — Broken Object Level Authorization (BOLA), the most common API bug
API2: OWASP API Security Top 10 risk #2 — Broken Authentication
API3: OWASP API Security Top 10 risk #3 — Broken Object Property Level Authorization (mass assignment, excessive data exposure)
API4: OWASP API Security Top 10 risk #4 — Unrestricted Resource Consumption
API5: OWASP API Security Top 10 risk #5 — Broken Function Level Authorization
API6: OWASP API Security Top 10 risk #6 — Unrestricted Access to Sensitive Business Flows
API7: OWASP API Security Top 10 risk #7 — Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF)
API8: OWASP API Security Top 10 risk #8 — Security Misconfiguration
API9: OWASP API Security Top 10 risk #9 — Improper Inventory Management (shadow and zombie APIs)
API10: OWASP API Security Top 10 risk #10 — Unsafe Consumption of APIs
OIDC: OpenID Connect, an identity layer built on top of OAuth 2.0 for user login
CAPTCHA: a challenge that tells humans from bots, used to blunt automated abuse
SAST: static application security testing, scanning source code for vulnerabilities
DAST: dynamic application security testing, scanning a running application for vulnerabilities
SOAP: Simple Object Access Protocol, an older XML-based web-service protocol where XXE still lurks
XML: Extensible Markup Language, a text data format; parsing it unsafely enables XXE attacks
XXE: XML External Entity, an attack that abuses an XML parser's external-entity feature to read files or make requests
ALPAC: Automatic Language Processing Advisory Committee, the US committee whose 1966 report led to machine-translation funding being cut
PEAS: performance measure, environment, actuators, sensors: the four-part description of an AI agent’s task
UCS: uniform-cost search, which always expands the cheapest path found so far
ART: Android Runtime, the runtime that runs Android apps; also adaptive resonance theory (machine learning), a family of neural networks that group data without labels
MLC: multi-level cell, flash memory that stores 2 bits per cell; also maximum likelihood classifier (machine learning), which assigns an example to the class under whose fitted distribution it is most likely
MLP: multilayer perceptron, a feed-forward neural network with one or more hidden layers
WEKA: Waikato Environment for Knowledge Analysis, a free data-mining tool with many ready-made classifiers
ISODATA: iterative self-organising data analysis technique, a clustering method like k-means that can also split and merge clusters
DOI: Digital Object Identifier: a permanent link to a published paper or dataset
FFP: fabrication, falsification, plagiarism: the three kinds of research misconduct
ICMJE: International Committee of Medical Journal Editors, whose authorship rules many fields use
HD: high definition: a screen 1,920 pixels wide and 1,080 tall
RGBA: red, green, blue, alpha: a colour as three amounts of light plus a fourth number for how see-through it is
UNISURF: Renault's 1960s computer system for designing car body surfaces, where Pierre Bézier used his curves
VR: virtual reality: a headset shows a computer-made 3D world all around you
AR: augmented reality: computer graphics drawn on top of your view of the real world
